On this page

Elastic waves ​

Plane waves of a homogeneous elastic medium, their first-order forms in a weakly anisotropic one, waves at a plane interface, and the small waves of a deformed solid. Theory: Plane waves, Thomsen's parameters, Weak anisotropy of any symmetry, Shear-wave splitting, Waves at an interface, Characteristic roots, Third-order elasticity; usage: Plane waves, Waves at an interface, Third-order elasticity.

Plane waves ​

TensND.PlaneWaves Type
julia
PlaneWaves{T}

The three plane waves of a direction direction (unit), sorted by decreasing phase velocity (qP, qS1, qS2): velocity[m] the phase velocity of the wave m, polarization[:, m] its unit polarization and group[:, m] its group velocity. Built by plane_waves.

TensND.plane_waves Function
julia
plane_waves(ℂ::AbstractTens{4,3}, ρ, n) → PlaneWaves

The three plane waves that travel along the direction n (any nonzero vector) in a medium of stiffness ℂ and mass density ρ: solutions of the Christoffel problem

sorted by decreasing phase velocity (qP, qS1, qS2), with their unit polarizations and their group velocities      (Plane waves). The components are canonical, whatever the basis ℂ is written in.

Numbers and dual numbers; the derivative of a polarization is left out between two waves of the same velocity, where it is not defined. A direction in which an eigenvalue is not positive throws a DomainError. For symbols see wave_modes and christoffel_invariants.

Examples

julia
julia> w = plane_waves(iso_stiffness(5.0, 2.0), 2.0, (0, 0, 1));

julia> w.velocity ≈ [sqrt((5 + 4 * 2 / 3) / 2), 1, 1]
true
TensND.phase_velocities Function
julia
phase_velocities(ℂ, ρ, n) → SVector{3}

The phase velocities of the three plane waves along n, in decreasing order (qP, qS1, qS2): the field velocity of plane_waves.

TensND.slowness Function
julia
slowness(w::PlaneWaves) → SMatrix{3,3}

The slowness vectors of the three waves, one per column.

TensND.wave_modes Function
julia
wave_modes(ℂ::TensISO{4,3}, ρ, n) → (P = (velocity, polarization), S = …)
wave_modes(ℂ::TensTI{4}, ρ, n) → (qP = …, qSV = …, SH = …)

The plane waves of an isotropic or of a transversely isotropic medium along n, in closed form and under the name of their mode, each as a pair (velocity, polarization). No velocity is compared with another: symbols go through, and a mode keeps its name where it crosses another.

Isotropic:    along , and   for every polarization normal to it (polarization is then nothing).

Transversely isotropic of axis , with the angle between and and the components in the usual two-index notation of the axis 3:

SH is polarized along  ; qP and qSV in the plane of and , given by their components (along the transverse direction, along the axis) in that plane, for a direction on the side of the axis,    (the direction carries the same waves) (Plane waves).

TensND.christoffel_invariants Function
julia
christoffel_invariants(ℂ::AbstractTens{4,3}, ρ, n) → (I₁, I₂, I₃)

The invariants of : its trace, the trace of its adjugate and its determinant. The squared phase velocities   along the unit direction n are the roots of

Polynomial in the components of ℂ and of n: numbers, dual numbers and symbols.

Thomsen's parameters and weak anisotropy ​

The form :thomsen of ti_from_constants and ti_constants builds a stiffness from these parameters and reads them back.

TensND.thomsen_parameters Function
julia
thomsen_parameters(t::TensTI{4}, ρ) → (V_P0, V_S0, ε, δ, γ)
thomsen_parameters(t::AbstractTens{4,3}, ρ; axis = nothing)

Thomsen's parameters of the transversely isotropic stiffness t of a medium of density ρ, as a named tuple: the velocities of the P and S waves along the axis, and

in the two-index notation of the axis 3. The definitions are exact; the parameters are small for a weakly anisotropic medium (Thomsen's parameters). It is ti_constants(t; form = :thomsen, density = ρ) with names; the converse is ti_from_constants(V_P0, V_S0, ε, δ, γ, axis; form = :thomsen, density = ρ).

Any other stiffness is accepted when it is transversely isotropic: an isotropic one about any axis ( by default), whose , and vanish; a tensor of another type about the axis given or, for numbers, about the axis found (project_exact). Otherwise the call is refused: the generalized parameters of generalized_thomsen_parameters hold for any symmetry.

TensND.anellipticity Function
julia
anellipticity(t::TensTI{4}) → η
anellipticity(t::AbstractTens{4,3}; axis = nothing)

The anellipticity     of a transversely isotropic stiffness: zero when the slowness curve of the P wave is an ellipse. It does not depend on the density. Another stiffness is taken as thomsen_parameters takes it.

TensND.weak_wave_modes Function
julia
weak_wave_modes(t::TensTI{4}, ρ, n) → (qP = V, qSV = V, SH = V)
weak_wave_modes(t::AbstractTens{4,3}, ρ, n; axis = nothing)

The phase velocities of the three modes along n to first order in Thomsen's parameters,

being the angle between n and the axis. wave_modes gives the exact velocities, of which these are the first-order series. Another stiffness is taken as thomsen_parameters takes it.

TensND.squared_moveout_velocities Function
julia
squared_moveout_velocities(t::TensTI{4}, ρ) → (qP = V², qSV = V², SH = V²)
squared_moveout_velocities(t::AbstractTens{4,3}, ρ; axis = nothing)

The squares of the short-spread moveout velocities of a horizontal reflector in a medium of vertical axis, exact for any strength of the anisotropy:  ,     and  , that is the squared velocity of each mode along its axis times one plus the second derivative, at the axis, of the logarithm of its phase velocity (Thomsen's parameters). The squares are returned because the qSV one is negative in many rocks (  large and negative): the travel time of the reflected qSV wave then decreases with the offset, and no moveout velocity exists. Another stiffness is taken as thomsen_parameters takes it.

TensND.weak_plane_waves Function
julia
weak_plane_waves(ℂ::AbstractTens{4,3}, ρ, n) → (qP = …, qS1 = …, qS2 = …)

The three plane waves along n to first order in the deviation of ℂ from isotropy, each as a pair (velocity, polarization):

where     on an orthonormal pair normal to . The P wave is polarized along , the S waves along the eigenvectors of the 2×2 problem (Weak anisotropy of any symmetry). The result does not depend on a reference medium. Numbers, dual numbers and symbols; plane_waves gives the exact waves.

TensND.generalized_thomsen_parameters Function
julia
generalized_thomsen_parameters(ℂ::AbstractTens{4,3}) → NamedTuple

The dimensionless parameters that describe, to first order, the velocities of a stiffness of any symmetry about the vertical , in the two-index notation of the canonical components (voigt_stiffness) and with the reference moduli of the vertical waves,   for P and , for the two S:

The fifteen first ones are the combinations of the stiffness that the P wave sees to first order; the index names the plane normal to that axis. For a transversely isotropic medium of axis they reduce to Thomsen's:   ,  , and   equals Thomsen's to first order (Weak anisotropy of any symmetry). Numbers, dual numbers and symbols.

TensND.shear_splitting Function
julia
shear_splitting(ℂ::AbstractTens{4,3}, ρ, n) → (splitting, fast, delay)

The splitting of the shear waves that travel along n:

  • splitting:  , between 0 and 1, the fast velocity as the reference;

  • fast: the unit polarization of the fast wave;

  • delay:  , the time by which the slow wave lags per unit length of path.

Read on plane_waves; numbers and dual numbers (Shear-wave splitting).

Waves at an interface ​

TensND.InterfaceWave Type
julia
InterfaceWave{T}

One of the six plane waves of a medium for a given tangential slowness: normal_slowness (ξ, complex), slowness (  ), polarization (unit, complex), traction (    ), flux ( , the mean energy flux through the interface per unit ) and homogeneous (true for a real ξ).

TensND.interface_waves Function
julia
interface_waves(ℂ::AbstractTens{4,3}, ρ, ν, sₜ) → (forward, backward)

The six plane waves of the medium of stiffness ℂ and density ρ whose slowness has the tangential part sₜ on the plane of unit normal ν (the part of sₜ along ν is removed): three forward waves, which carry energy or decay towards , and three backward ones, as tuples of InterfaceWave sorted by increasing normal slowness in absolute value (the fastest wave, quasi-longitudinal, first).

A homogeneous wave (real normal slowness) is classed by the sign of the normal component of its energy flux; an evanescent one by the sign of the imaginary part of its normal slowness, positive when it decays towards . The angle beyond which a wave turns evanescent is its critical angle (Waves at an interface).

Two homogeneous waves of the same normal slowness (the two shear waves of an isotropic medium) share a plane of polarizations, of which any orthonormal pair solves the problem: the pair returned is the one whose energy fluxes add. Their individual amplitudes in reflection_transmission depend on that choice; the field and the energy they carry together do not.

Numbers and dual numbers. An isotropic stiffness with symbols (Symbolics.Num) gives the six waves in closed form, below the critical angles and for a nonzero tangential slowness: no root is compared there, the forward waves are those of positive normal slowness.

TensND.reflection_transmission Function
julia
reflection_transmission(ℂ₁, ρ₁, ℂ₂, ρ₂, ν, incident::InterfaceWave; slip = nothing)
    → (reflected, transmitted, R, T, energy)

The waves that the incident wave, one of the forward waves of the medium 1 (interface_waves, on the side   ), excites at the plane interface with the medium 2: the three reflected waves of the medium 1 and the three transmitted waves of the medium 2, with their complex amplitudes R and T per unit incident amplitude (displacement amplitudes, unit polarizations) and energy, the fractions of the incident energy flux carried by each of the six waves (zero for an evanescent wave): they sum to one.

The interface is welded, displacement and traction continuous. With slip, a 3×3 matrix (angular frequency times a compliance of the interface), the displacement jumps by times the traction (linear slip); the traction stays continuous (Waves at an interface). Numbers and dual numbers.

TensND.free_surface_reflection Function
julia
free_surface_reflection(ℂ::AbstractTens{4,3}, ρ, ν, incident::InterfaceWave) → (reflected, R, energy)

The waves that the incident wave, one of the forward waves of the medium (interface_waves, on the side   ), excites at the free surface   : the three reflected waves, their complex amplitudes R per unit incident amplitude (unit polarizations) and energy, the fractions of the incident energy flux they carry, which sum to one. The traction vanishes on the surface,

(Waves at an interface). Numbers and dual numbers.

TensND.weak_contrast_reflection Function
julia
weak_contrast_reflection(ℂ, ρ, δℂ, δρ, ν, incident::InterfaceWave) → (reflected, R)

The reflection coefficients, to first order in the contrast, at the welded interface between the medium of the incident wave and the medium   : with the waves of the first medium only, incident and reflected,

being the change of the displacement and traction of the incident wave when its medium becomes the second one, written without its polarization change (Waves at an interface). Valid for any anisotropy, the incident wave a simple root. Numbers, dual numbers, and symbols where the waves are symbolic.

Characteristic roots of a stiffness of the plane ​

TensND.engineering_compliances Function
julia
engineering_compliances(ℂ::AbstractTens{4,2}) → (a₁₁, a₂₂, a₁₂, a₆₆, a₁₆, a₂₆)

The compliances of the stiffness ℂ of the plane in the engineering form, in the canonical axes:

TensND.characteristic_pair Function
julia
characteristic_pair(ℂ::AbstractTens{4,2}) → (s, p)

Sum    and product   of the two characteristic roots of positive imaginary part of the stiffness ℂ of the plane, in the canonical axes: the roots of

with the engineering compliances of the plane (Characteristic roots).

An isotropic tensor has the double root , hence  ; an orthotropic or a square one has the pair of its own axes in closed form, turned to the canonical ones: these three accept symbols. Any other tensor has its equation solved numerically (numbers and dual numbers), and must be major-symmetric. See characteristic_roots.

TensND.characteristic_roots Function
julia
characteristic_roots(ℂ::AbstractTens{4,2}) → (μ₁, μ₂)

The two characteristic roots of positive imaginary part of the stiffness ℂ of the plane, from their sum and product (characteristic_pair):   . Near an isotropic tensor the two roots merge and are not differentiable functions of the stiffness, while their sum and product are: a computation that must stay smooth is written with the pair.

Third-order elasticity ​

TensND.ThirdOrderIsotropic Type
julia
ThirdOrderIsotropic(λ, μ, l, m, n)

A hyperelastic solid isotropic at orders two and three: Lamé's constants λ, μ and Murnaghan's third-order constants l, m, n, of the strain energy

in the Green–Lagrange strain (Third-order elasticity). Numbers, dual numbers and symbols. See third_order_constants for the other notations.

TensND.third_order_constants Function
julia
third_order_constants(s::ThirdOrderIsotropic) → (C111, C112, C123, A, B, C)

The third-order constants of s in the two other usual notations: the components   ,  ,     of the sixth-order tensor in the two-index notation, and Landau's  ,   ,    .

TensND.third_order_from_constants Function
julia
third_order_from_constants(λ, μ, C₁₁₁, C₁₁₂, C₁₂₃) → ThirdOrderIsotropic

The solid of Lamé's constants λ, μ and of the third-order constants given in the two-index notation: Murnaghan's  ,    and     , the converse of third_order_constants.

TensND.strain_energy Function
julia
strain_energy(s::ThirdOrderIsotropic, E) → W

The strain energy of s per unit reference volume for the Green–Lagrange strain E, a symmetric 3×3 matrix of canonical components.

TensND.cauchy_stress Function
julia
cauchy_stress(s::ThirdOrderIsotropic, F) → SMatrix{3,3}

The Cauchy stress     of s under the deformation gradient F.

TensND.tangent_stiffness Function
julia
tangent_stiffness(s::ThirdOrderIsotropic, E) → AbstractTens{4,3}

The tangent   of the second Piola–Kirchhoff stress of s at the Green–Lagrange strain E (a symmetric 3×3 matrix of canonical components):

with     ,    and    : the isotropic stiffness of λ, μ plus a term linear in E. It has the minor and major symmetries (Third-order elasticity).

TensND.acoustoelastic_tensor Function
julia
acoustoelastic_tensor(s::ThirdOrderIsotropic, F) → AbstractTens{4,3}

The tensor   that governs a small motion superposed on the static deformation of gradient F (a 3×3 matrix of canonical components), in the reference coordinates:

with    , the second Piola–Kirchhoff stress and its tangent (tangent_stiffness). It has the major symmetry and, under stress, not the minor ones. For   it is the isotropic stiffness of λ, μ.

TensND.prestressed_waves Function
julia
prestressed_waves(s::ThirdOrderIsotropic, ρ₀, F, N) → PlaneWaves

The three small plane waves of reference direction N in the solid s, of reference density ρ₀, under the static deformation of gradient F: natural velocities (a reference length over a travel time), sorted by decreasing value, and polarizations, the eigenpairs of     (acoustoelastic_tensor). The field group holds the natural group velocities     . Numbers and dual numbers.

TensND.acoustoelastic_coefficients Function
julia
acoustoelastic_coefficients(s::ThirdOrderIsotropic)

The first-order effect of a stress on the velocities of s, in closed form (Johnson & Rasolofosaon 1996, Eqs. (18)–(20), after Hughes & Kelly 1953): the derivatives of (reference density, true velocity , a length of the deformed solid over a travel time) with respect to a compressive stress , taken at  ,

  • P_parallel, S_parallel: uniaxial stress along the direction of propagation;

  • P_perpendicular, S_perpendicular_parallel, S_perpendicular_perpendicular: uniaxial stress normal to it, the shear wave being polarized along the stress or normal to it;

  • P_hydrostatic, S_hydrostatic: pressure ;

and the two coefficients of the anisotropy that a uniaxial stress induces, at the angle between propagation and stress,

a_P and b_S ( polarized in the plane of the stress and of the propagation, normal to it). Derivation in Third-order elasticity. Numbers, dual numbers and symbols.

TensND.strain_stiffening Function
julia
strain_stiffening(s::ThirdOrderIsotropic, E) → AbstractTens{4,3}

The change of stiffness that the strain E (a symmetric 3×3 matrix of canonical components) brings about through the third-order constants of s,  :

that is     and its companions in the two-index notation for principal strains. It does not depend on λ and μ: added to the stiffness of an anisotropic background, it is the model of Prioul et al. (2004) for a rock whose anisotropy at rest is not isotropic while its nonlinearity is (Third-order elasticity).
